added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs: the after arm (logs/suite-head.log, revision c3852b403, completed to its summary line, 8550 passed 0 failed 11 skipped, EXIT=0) carries no failing id at all, so no failure can have been added; the baseline arm (logs/suite-base.log) is truncated at 58% with no summary line and no EXIT= line, so it contributes no ids and cannot be read as the source of the five ids the manifest attributes to it.

findings.text: The reviewed worktree .../sib-drained-queue-exit is left with this change reverted in the working tree AND in the index: `git -C <worktree> diff --cached HEAD` shows the 14-line sn.py block and the 12-line graph_parent_lifecycle.py block deleted (`grep -c source_claim_where` is 2 at HEAD, 0 in the tree). HEAD c3852b403 is correct, but an interrupted base-arm suite run (stream record at line 7336, killed with exit 137 before its restore line) left the tree on the base product files. Any commit made in that worktree -- including a merge concluded there, which takes the whole index -- lands the revert, so the change is intact only until someone commits from that tree. Repair by `git -C <worktree> checkout HEAD -- imas_codex/cli/sn.py imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_parent_lifecycle.py` (the fix lives in HEAD), or reclaim the worktree before any commit.

The claimability predicate is now written out as literal Cypher in three places -- the owner `claim_generate_name_batch` at imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_cost_and_claims.py:486/506 and both pending counts (imas_codex/cli/sn.py:616 and here) -- with no shared constant. The count drifting from the claim is exactly the defect this node repaired, and the fix re-states the predicate rather than extracting it, so the next change to the claim predicate can reintroduce the same divergence silently. A module-level fragment exported beside `_PIPELINE_FROZEN_NAME_STAGES` and interpolated by all three sites would close it; the graph_store sibling-import rule that forced commit 07e795a68 is satisfied by exporting it from graph_foundation or the wired services namespace.

`baseline_suite` declares `completed: true`, but the log it cites (logs/suite-base.log) is truncated at 58% of the progress bar: 80 lines, no pytest summary line, no `EXIT=` line, and only the single `F` already printed at 48%. The run it describes is the third base-arm attempt, which the worker's own stream shows was killed with exit code 137 before the shell appended its exit line; the completed base-arm measurement (5 failed, 8545 passed) was a previous attempt whose log was overwritten. The declared failure_ids are consistent with that earlier run, and the added-failure answer is unaffected because the after arm names zero failures, but the receipt as written cannot be re-read to confirm it.

The two modified Cypher statements were never executed or explained against a live engine: `-m graph` is never passed and no `EXPLAIN` appears anywhere in the run's stream. The repo's graph guidance requires one of them for edited Cypher, because the default markers exclude the graph marker and a syntax error therefore surfaces only when a live run's watchdog calls the count. The risk is low in fact -- every construct used (`EXISTS { MATCH ... }`, `NOT EXISTS { MATCH ... WHERE ... }`, `$frozen_name_stages` list parameter) already parses in live statements in the same files -- but the statement itself is unproven.

The docstring cites `job 1308077`, a transient scheduler job id that no longer resolves and means nothing to a reader without access to that job's record. The user-global naming rule bans tracker/job/RCA references in source comments and docstrings; the numbers that matter here (101 derived plus 3 manual, 104 pending, none carrying a DD path) are already stated in the same docstring and stand on their own.

justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in the diff -- imas_codex/cli/sn.py, imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_parent_lifecycle.py, tests/standard_names/test_drained_queue_exit.py and the evidence fragment -- is inside the six declared write paths and no other file is touched.
